# @audaxic/memory-opencode

OpenCode plugin for [Audaxic Memory](https://memory.audaxic.com) — automatically saves conversation facts to your persistent memory layer and injects relevant memories as context before the agent answers.

Supports **OpenCode v1 (1.18.29+)** and **OpenCode v2 (2.x)** from a single package: v1 loads the `server`/`tui` entrypoints, v2 loads the `setup` entrypoints.

## Installation

```bash
npm install -g @audaxic/memory-opencode
```

## Setup

Before using the plugin, configure your API key:

```bash
npx @audaxic/memory-opencode setup
```

This will prompt for your Audaxic general API key and save it to `~/.config/audaxic/config.json` with secure file permissions (600). It also offers to save a separate key for the current project directory.

Get your API key from: https://memory-dashboard.audaxic.com

## Configuration

### OpenCode v2 (2.x)

Add to your `opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@audaxic/memory-opencode"]
}
```

The sidebar widget is loaded automatically from the package's `./tui` entrypoint.

### OpenCode v1 — server plugin

Add to your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@audaxic/memory-opencode"]
}
```

### OpenCode v1 — TUI plugin (sidebar indicator + toast)

Add to your `~/.config/opencode/tui.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
  "plugin": ["@audaxic/memory-opencode"]
}
```

The plugin will be automatically loaded by OpenCode on startup.

## How It Works

1. **Message Capture:** V1 uses the `chat.message` hook and the `message.part.updated` event; V2 uses the `prompt` session hook and the `session.text.ended` event.

2. **Immediate Save:** Each captured message is written to a unique parking file under `~/.config/audaxic/pending/` (milliseconds) — hooks never wait on the network. A background sender posts files to `POST /add` (30s timeout, 3 concurrent) without blocking the conversation. Messages larger than the API's 15,000-character per-message limit are split into newline-aligned chunks before sending.

3. **Crash Safety:** A message's parking file is deleted **only after the API confirms receipt**. On any failure (HTTP error, timeout, network exception) the file stays on disk and is retried automatically — data loss is impossible.

4. **Recovery:** A periodic tick (every 60s) and a startup scan retry parked files older than 60 seconds. Files are claimed atomically (safe rename) before sending, and abandoned claims older than 5 minutes are healed back for retry. Claiming never reads or writes a file another process owns, so recovery is safe with multiple sessions running.

5. **Parallel-Safe:** Every message gets its own file — multiple OpenCode sessions and processes never share or overwrite the same file.

6. **Silent Failure:** If no API key is configured, the plugin logs a warning and disables itself without blocking OpenCode.

## Version Support

| OpenCode | Config | Entrypoints |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| v2 (2.x) | `plugins` in `opencode.jsonc` | `setup` (server) + `./tui` (CLI, automatic) |
| v1 (1.18.29+) | `plugin` in `opencode.json` + `tui.json` | `server` + `tui` |

Notes:
- V1 releases older than 1.18.29 cannot load the dual entrypoint; use a previous package version there.
- The sidebar status bridge between the server plugin and the TUI is file-based (`~/.config/audaxic/status/`). It works with a locally spawned server; with a remote v2 server the widget will not see status updates.
- In V2, the `prompt` hook runs before prompt admission, so a prompt that is later rejected may still have been saved to memory.

## Diagnostics

The server plugin never writes to the terminal (terminal output corrupts the TUI). All diagnostics go to `~/.config/audaxic/hook.log` with ISO timestamps — check it for search/`/add` failures. A missing parking file on startup is normal and never logged.

## Sidebar Indicator

The TUI plugin adds a status block to the session sidebar, reading a per-session status file:

| State | Display |
|-------|---------|
| Idle | `● Audaxic Memory` / `listening` |
| Saved | `● Audaxic Memory` / `saved` (brief, after each message) |
| Searching | `● Audaxic Memory` / `retrieving...` |
| Retrieved | `● Audaxic Memory` / `retrieved 3 memories` (brief) |
| Error | `● Audaxic Memory` / `last save failed` (yellow) |

The indicator updates every 2 seconds by polling the status files. Each session's sidebar shows its own session's status, even with multiple OpenCode instances running.

## Environment Variable Alternative

Instead of using the setup script, you can set the API key as an environment variable:

```bash
export AUDAXIC_API_KEY="ak_your_key_here"
```

The plugin checks in this order:
1. `AUDAXIC_API_KEY` environment variable
2. `directoryKeys` entry matching the OpenCode workspace directory
3. `~/.config/audaxic/config.json` general `apiKey`

## Directory-specific API keys

Give each project its own memory project by mapping a directory to an API key. The key is scoped to one project on the server, so opening a directory uses that project automatically.

```bash
# General fallback used outside mapped directories
npx @audaxic/memory-opencode key set --global

# Inside a project directory: use that project's key
cd C:\projeler\my-project
npx @audaxic/memory-opencode key set

# Inspect
npx @audaxic/memory-opencode key list
npx @audaxic/memory-opencode key resolve
```

The shared config looks like this:

```json
{
  "apiKey": "ak_general...",
  "directoryKeys": {
    "C:\\projeler\\my-project": "ak_project_a...",
    "C:\\projeler\\another-project": "ak_project_b..."
  }
}
```

Matching uses the nearest parent directory, so opening `my-project/packages/api` uses the `my-project` key unless a more specific entry exists. Git worktrees fall back to the main checkout's key; a worktree-specific entry overrides it. The config is stored in your user profile with mode `0600`; keys are never written into a repository.

Same directory means the same memory project across Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. In OpenCode v2 one background service can serve multiple workspaces, so the plugin resolves the key per workspace and stores the key with every parked message. A message captured in workspace A is always sent to A's project, even if another workspace drains it.

## Memory Search & Context Injection

After a user prompt is received and **before** the agent answers, the plugin:

1. Takes the latest user message (excluding synthetic parts like file-read output).
2. Searches your memory via `POST /search` (up to 5 results, 15s timeout, 2 attempts, IPv4-first DNS for reliability).
3. Injects the results as a synthetic user message wrapped in `<audaxic_memory_context>...</audaxic_memory_context>` into the model request.

The injection is:
- **In-memory only** — it never persists to the session, so you won't see it in the conversation history or TUI (V1 injects a synthetic user message for the model request; V2 adds a text part to the model request's system context, re-applied on every request of the turn so memories survive tool loops).
- **Once per user message** — the memory search runs once per prompt; later requests reuse the results instead of re-searching.
- **Silent on failure** — if the search API is unreachable, the plugin logs a warning and the conversation proceeds without context.

To disable auto-search/injection (saving still works):

```bash
export AUDAXIC_SEARCH=off
```

## API Endpoints

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `https://api.memory.audaxic.com/add` | POST | Save conversation messages |
| `https://api.memory.audaxic.com/search` | POST | Search memories for context injection |
